IVX AUTONOMOUS 24/7 — 9/10 TO ENTERPRISE STABILITY

MODE: CONTINUOUS ENGINEERING EXECUTION
PRIORITY: STABILITY BEFORE FEATURES
OWNER MODEL: PERIODIC SUPERVISION, NOT DAILY MICROMANAGEMENT

OBJECTIVE

Operate IVX Autonomous continuously, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, to stabilize, clean, test, document and improve the complete IVX engineering platform from its current condition toward enterprise-grade reliability.

Work one verified gap at a time.

Do not process all defects in one oversized task.
Do not stop the entire engineering program because one external credential or approval is unavailable.
Continue every other safe task that can be completed independently.

==================================================
1. CANONICAL OWNER-CONTROLLED BASELINE
==================================================

Use only:

Repository:
ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Production branch:
main

Production service:
Render service srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0

Approved production lifecycle:

isolated branch
→ code change
→ regression test
→ commit
→ push
→ pull request
→ CI
→ owner approval
→ merge
→ Render deployment
→ /health verification
→ /version verification
→ SHA parity
→ evidence ledger

Never modify main directly.

Never deploy production from ivx-autonomous.

Never use a local Rork workspace as the production source of truth.

==================================================
2. ACCESS RECOVERY — FIRST ACTIVE TASK
==================================================

Repair and verify the execution authentication context.

Audit:

- GitHub repository access
- GitHub Contents read/write
- Pull Requests read/write
- GitHub Actions read/write
- Workflow read/write
- branch-protection read access
- Render deployment read/write
- IVX owner-runtime authentication

For every connection return only:

- connection
- PASS/FAIL
- authentication type
- permission available
- exact blocker
- exact owner action, only when unavoidable

Do not expose credentials.

Attempt to recover existing owner-controlled connections before requesting new credentials.

Required initial result:

GITHUB_AUTH_VERIFIED
RENDER_AUTH_VERIFIED
IVX_OWNER_RUNTIME_VERIFIED

If one connection remains unavailable, mark only that task:

BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL

Continue all safe local engineering tasks that do not require that connection.

==================================================
3. DURABLE ENGINEERING BACKLOG
==================================================

Create a persistent prioritized backlog.

Each item must contain:

- task ID
- defect/gap ID
- title
- module
- severity
- risk
- dependencies
- selected files
- branch
- current status
- tests
- commit SHA
- PR URL
- CI run ID
- deployment ID
- verification evidence
- owner approval required
- next action

Statuses:

- QUEUED
- INSPECTING
- REPRODUCING
- EDITING
- TESTING
- REPAIRING
- PR_OPEN
- CI_RUNNING
- WAITING_OWNER_APPROVAL
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING
- VERIFIED
- BLOCKED_CREDENTIAL
- BLOCKED_OWNER_APPROVAL
- FAILED
- ROLLED_BACK

Never mark VERIFIED because code or a commit merely exists.

==================================================
4. EXACT PRIORITY ORDER
==================================================

Execute work in this order:

P0 — SECURITY AND SOURCE CONTROL

1. Remove every direct-write path to main.
2. Block Git Data API updates to refs/heads/main.
3. Remove overridable production target branches.
4. Confirm Render deploys only from main.
5. Remove hard-coded owner credentials.
6. Standardize owner authentication.
7. Remove secret exposure.
8. Prove zero active Rork production dependency.

P0 — CI/CD AND DEPLOYMENT INTEGRITY

9. Restore authenticated GitHub Actions access.
10. Restore continuous runner heartbeat.
11. Reconcile a clean canonical main checkout.
12. Fix Expo/Gradle version consistency.
13. Fix workflow and runner failures.
14. Require a real Render deployment ID.
15. Require GitHub/CI/Render/runtime SHA parity.
16. Prevent false COMPLETED statuses.
17. Implement rollback and restart recovery.

P1 — AUTONOMOUS WORKER RELIABILITY

18. Fix request attachment and job replacement.
19. Add duplicate-request idempotency.
20. Preserve CANCELLED status correctly.
21. Revalidate approvals before resume.
22. Make conversation-state writes atomic.
23. Expand zombie detection to every execution stage.
24. Make durable storage authoritative.
25. Remove ephemeral file state as production authority.

P1 — PRODUCT STABILITY

26. Owner login and session persistence.
27. Member registration.
28. Investor/buyer/JV/tokenized registration.
29. IVX IA chat loading and history.
30. Duplicate and out-of-order chat prevention.
31. Reels and media stability.
32. Uploads and notifications.
33. Android startup and crash recovery.
34. iOS startup and crash recovery.
35. API and database reliability.

P2 — QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

36. TypeScript.
37. Lint.
38. Broken imports.
39. Dead and duplicate code.
40. Dependency cleanup.
41. Test coverage.
42. Performance.
43. Security hardening.
44. Architecture documentation.
45. Technical debt.

Do not prioritize new features while P0 or P1 defects remain.

==================================================
5. ONE GAP PER EXECUTION BATCH
==================================================

For each backlog item:

1. Select exactly one defect.
2. Identify exact file, function and root cause.
3. Create:

   auto-fix/<task-id>-<short-name>

4. Add a regression test that reproduces the defect.
5. Confirm the test fails before repair.
6. Apply the smallest safe change.
7. Run focused tests.
8. Run TypeScript.
9. Run lint for affected files.
10. Run relevant integration/E2E tests.
11. Scan changed files for secrets.
12. Review the diff.
13. Commit.
14. Push.
15. Open a PR.
16. Monitor CI.
17. Repair only failures caused by that change.
18. Record evidence.
19. Continue to the next safe task.

Never combine unrelated defects in one PR.

Maximum recommended scope:

- one defect;
- one module;
- limited related files;
- one independently reviewable PR.

==================================================
6. SAFE AUTONOMOUS AUTHORITY
==================================================

Autonomous is authorized without repeated owner approval to:

- inspect repositories
- create branches
- edit non-destructive code
- add regression tests
- run TypeScript
- run lint
- run tests
- repair CI
- repair workflows
- remove dead or duplicate code
- improve internal architecture safely
- commit
- push
- open PRs
- monitor CI
- prepare deployment evidence
- create reports

Owner approval is required before:

- production deployment
- database migration
- RLS modification
- authentication behavior change
- payment modification
- destructive data action
- secret rotation
- Android/iOS production signing
- AWS/DNS/Render/Supabase infrastructure mutation
- destructive architectural migration

A blocked high-risk task must not stop unrelated safe work.

==================================================
7. CI STABILITY GATE
==================================================

Required workflows:

- IVX CI
- IVX QA Suite
- IVX E2E Acceptance Pipeline
- Android Emulator QA
- iOS Simulator QA

For each failure:

- capture run ID
- capture runner
- capture first failed step
- capture exact error
- identify root cause
- fix in isolated branch
- add regression coverage
- rerun affected workflow

Final stability target:

- all five workflows execute on real runners;
- all critical jobs PASS;
- three consecutive successful runs;
- no skipped critical jobs;
- no anonymous private-repository verification;
- no production credentials in ordinary unit tests.

==================================================
8. DEPLOYMENT COMPLETION GATE
==================================================

A production task may be marked VERIFIED only when all exist:

- owner approval ID
- branch
- commit SHA
- remote SHA
- PR URL
- CI-tested SHA
- merge SHA
- Render deployment ID
- Render status LIVE
- /health HTTP 200
- /version HTTP 200
- production smoke test
- verification timestamp

Required equality:

GitHub main SHA
=
CI-tested SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

If any item is missing:

- do not mark COMPLETED;
- use the truthful blocked or failed status;
- preserve the evidence;
- keep rollback available.

==================================================
9. SELF-DIAGNOSIS AND SAFE SELF-REPAIR
==================================================

Continuously monitor:

- application crashes
- API 4xx/5xx spikes
- authentication failures
- Render failures
- GitHub Actions failures
- Supabase failures
- stuck jobs
- missing heartbeat
- SHA mismatches
- duplicate chat messages
- blank screens
- infinite loading
- upload failures
- notification failures
- mobile startup failures
- dependency failures
- latency regressions

Each incident must create:

- incident ID
- trace ID
- severity
- affected module
- current SHA
- stack trace
- occurrence count
- suspected file/function
- mitigation
- assigned repair task
- final evidence

Self-repair lifecycle:

detect
→ preserve evidence
→ reproduce
→ create branch
→ add regression test
→ repair
→ test
→ PR
→ CI
→ approval when required
→ deploy
→ verify
→ close incident

Never promise zero crashes.

Required behavior:

- detect rapidly;
- contain safely;
- roll back when a new release causes failure;
- repair through the controlled engineering pipeline;
- report actual measured recovery times.

==================================================
10. ANDROID AND IOS
==================================================

QA signing:

- temporary disposable debug signer;
- generated inside runner;
- never used for production.

Production signing:

- owner-controlled release keystore;
- protected GitHub environment secrets;
- encrypted owner backup;
- no release fallback to debug signing.

Do not block safe code cleanup while production signing awaits owner configuration.

Run Android and iOS automated QA continuously.

Request owner action only when physical-device testing or production signing is truly required.

==================================================
11. CONTINUOUS 24/7 LOOP
==================================================

Repeat continuously:

1. Check production health.
2. Check worker heartbeat.
3. Check CI.
4. Check incident queue.
5. Select highest-priority unblocked task.
6. Execute one safe repair batch.
7. Open PR.
8. Monitor CI.
9. Record evidence.
10. Select the next safe task.

When one task is blocked:

- record the blocker;
- notify the owner once;
- continue with the next independent safe task.

Do not pause the complete Autonomous program because one task is blocked.

==================================================
12. OWNER REPORTING
==================================================

Post a concise IVX IA Chat report every two hours:

- completed tasks
- active task
- queued P0/P1 tasks
- branches
- PRs
- CI run IDs
- failures
- GitHub SHA
- Render SHA
- runtime SHA
- incidents
- rollbacks
- blocked owner actions
- next three tasks

Post executive reports:

- 7:00 AM
- 7:00 PM

Send immediate alerts only for:

- production outage
- security incident
- data-loss risk
- failed rollback
- failed production deployment
- missing critical credential
- owner approval required

Do not repeat the same narrative report.

==================================================
13. FIRST THREE TASKS
==================================================

START NOW WITH THESE TASKS IN ORDER:

TASK 1 — AUTH-001
Restore owner-controlled GitHub and Render execution access.

TASK 2 — SCM-001
Block every direct mutation to main and require branch/PR/CI.

TASK 3 — CI-001
Fix the current Expo/Gradle Android version mismatch and execute the required CI workflows.

Complete each task separately.

Do not send all three as one oversized implementation.

==================================================
14. AUTONOMOUS ACTIVE ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

Return:

AUTONOMOUS_24_7_ACTIVE_VERIFIED

only when:

- durable backlog exists;
- worker heartbeat is active;
- GitHub/Render access is verified or correctly isolated as a blocker;
- first safe engineering task is executing;
- branch and job ID exist;
- reports are scheduled;
- blocked tasks do not stop safe tasks;
- main remains protected;
- no false completion claims occur.

Otherwise return:

AUTONOMOUS_24_7_PARTIALLY_ACTIVE

with:

- exact active task;
- completed safe work;
- exact blocker;
- next independent task already started.

START NOW WITH TASK AUTH-001.
CONTINUE ONE TASK AT A TIME.
DO NOT PAUSE THE ENTIRE PROGRAM FOR ONE BLOCKER.
DO NOT CREATE NEW PRODUCT FEATURES UNTIL STABILITY IS VERIFIED.
